One IC might drive 4 ICs while a different IC can only drive 2 ICs.

text: TTL family ICs are grouped together because they all share similar characteristics.
TTL ICs typically require input voltages between 0 and 5 volts. Voltage inputs exceeding 5 volts may damage the IC.
Output voltages produced by TTL ICs range between 0 and 5 volts. These outputs are designed to interface with other TTL Ics.m
Another characteristic of the TTL family is the current required to operate the IC.
The "fan-out" of a TTL IC identifies how many other ICs can be driven from it's output.
For example, if the ICs fan-out is 5, then 5 ICs could be connected to the output of that IC.
The "fan-in" of a TTL IC identifies how much current it will draw when driven by an IC similar to itself.
For example, if an ICs fan-in is 1, that value is subtracted from the fan-out of the driving IC.
The remaining value of 4 identifies that the driving ICs fan-out is now 4.
Speed is an important characteristic to compare when looking at the TTL family.

text: Notice, each TTL IC shown has a letter code included with the number. The letter identifies the speed of the IC.
ICs must switch from one condition (high) to the other condition (low). The time required for switching is indicated in the letter code.
An "L" in the IC number identifies Low Power consumption of that chip.
However, since nothing comes for free, these chips have slower switching speeds causing Longer propagation delays..r propagation delays.
An "H" in the IC number identifies a High speed switching or short propagation delay.
However, to achieve these higher switching speeds, more power is consumed.
An "S" in the IC number identifies Schottky circuitry inside.
Schottky ICs are Super fast and consume less power than most H-type Ics.
The amount of noise an IC makes when it switches from one condition to the other is also a characteristic.
The TTL Family of ICs produce noise each time they switch from high to low, or low to high.
If too much noise is introduced by IC switching, the input or output conditions can change at the wrong time.

text: This completes the information on TTL INTEGRATED CIRCUITS..
1. Transistor-Transistor Logic (TTL) is the most widely used family of integrated circuits.
2. The TTL family is divided into two basic groups.

items.label: 2. The TTL family is divided into two basic groups.

text: 3. Input and output voltages for TTL Family ICs range from 0 to 5V.

items.label: 3. Input and output voltages for TTL Family ICs range from 0 to 5V.

text: 4. Fan-in is a value given to an IC to represent the current it draws from a driven IC.
5. Fan-out is a value given to an IC to represent how many ICs, similar to itself, it can drive.
6. Speed is measured by propagation delay which is the amount of time an IC takes to switch from one condition to the other.

Three of the most common are CMOS, ECL and IIL. Let's discuss CMOS first.
Complementary MOS (CMOS) is slower than TTL but has a much lower power requirement than TTL.
CMOS is constructed from P and N-channel transistors to give the CMOS IC a high input impedance.

text: A high input impedance insures that the CMOS IC operates at a low input power.
As a technician you can identify a CMOS IC from a TTL IC by the "C" in the chip's number.
The major difference between TTL and CMOS is that CMOS input/output voltages range from 0 to 15 volts.
A major advantage of CMOS over TTL is noise. Almost no switching noise is generated by the CMOS IC.
Two other families you may encounter are ECL and IIL.......
The ECL family or Emitter-Coupled Logic is used in areas where speed is more important than cost.
The ECL Family is recognized most often by 10000 series numbers.
The IIL family or Integrated Injection Logic is used in circuits that require analog and digital interaction.
The IIL Family is recognized more easily from the manufacturers name than by the number of the IC.
There are different families of ICs because some circuits require speed while others require less power.
The TTL and IIL Families have an average tradeoff between speed and power.
CMOS trades the advantage of a very low power requirement for a disadvantage of a slow switching speed.
ECL trades the advantage of a very fast switching speed for the disadvantage of a very high power requirement.
Learn to use the IC data book, technical guide and cross reference manual when replacing a defective IC. Especially if you intend to substitute a replacement IC for the original.nt IC ...........
Replacing a defective 74F00 IC with a 74L00 IC may not repair the circuit, and can cause new problems.
